Our embedded firmware team has a C++ project under `ecu_firmware/` that we need to get into a proper state for our code intelligence toolchain. The project currently has no configuration for the toolchain, and the source files are completely unformatted (the team committed them without any style enforcement).

Please do the following:
1. Set up the project so our code intelligence toolchain can understand it — it needs a project-level configuration file (`.clangd`) that enforces C++17, enables all warnings (`-Wall` and `-Wextra`), strips conflicting warning flags, and activates strict checking for both unused and missing includes.
2. Produce a `compile_commands.json` build database at the project root so the toolchain knows how to build each file (it must include C++17 as the standard).
3. Apply consistent, automatic code formatting to all the `.cpp` and `.hpp` files under `src/` and `include/` in-place.
4. Run the static analyzer over the main source file (`src/throttle_controller.cpp`) to surface any issues.
5. Verify the whole thing still compiles cleanly with full warnings enabled.

The project lives at `/workspace/ecu_firmware/`.
